newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open weaker ahead of 10-year auction.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open weaker ahead of 10-year auction.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Wednesday, underperforming U.S. Treasuries amid a weaker dollar, profit-taking on recent spread narrowing and the pressure of today's 10-year bond auction, analysts said.

"It's more of a supply pressure thing going on here, combined with a weaker Canadian dollar and the fact that spreads did get in pretty tight," said Michael Gregory, a fixed-income economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers Canada Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.68 to C$110.70 to yield 7.093 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.91 percent. The spread between the two bonds widened to 18 basis points from 17 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.

Canadian bonds began the session lower amid some overnight selling in Europe ahead of this afternoon's 10-year auction. The Canadian government this afternoon will auction C$2.4 billion of bonds with a coupon of 7.25 percent and maturing on June 1, 2007. Results of the auction will be released at 1315/1715.
The selling of bonds helped weaken the currency, which in turn fed back into the bond market.
Canada's dollar opened slightly weaker in thin trading at C$1.3797 (US$0.7247) on Wednesday after heavy two-way activity overnight in overseas markets.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bonds fell C$0.60 to C$103.00 to yield 6.571 percent. The U.S. bond fell 9/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 14 basis points from 16 basis points on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.06 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.29 percent.
